Mark —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a tight MAP and a short checklist (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx and DPA-minimums-checklist.txt) that maps dependencies to decision owners. TL;DR on sequencing and options: 

Option A (recommended):
- Step 1 (Day 0–3): DPA signature (privacy + residency confirmed) — owner: NovAlign Legal / Redwood Legal.
- Step 2 (Day 0–5): Parallel commercial redlines: MSA redline exchange + Order Form pricing alignment — owner: Commercial teams.
- Step 3 (Day 6–10): MSA finalization and sign-off. Order Form held in draft until MSA approved but pricing table is agreed in parallel to avoid rework.
- Step 4 (Post-signature Day 0–14): Acceptance window (pilot & end-to-end checklists). Payment milestone tied to acceptance completion.

Why Option A: keeps privacy gating first, but reduces time-to-close by working redlines in parallel rather than strictly serial. The only blocker is major MSA structural changes; small redlines OK to parallelize.

Option B (conservative): Strict serial — no Order Form signature until MSA fully executed. Safest for legal, slower for procurement.

Risks we flagged in the MAP:
- If DPA requests data residency changes that require infra work, acceptance and pilot schedule will slip (owner: Redwood infra + PM).
- If MSA introduces payment terms changes (e.g., staged billing not aligned with our SKU model), pricing reconciliation may require commercial uplift.

Please see the attached one-pager for a lane-by-lane responsibility matrix. If you want, I can convert the MAP to a Visio timeline for distribution to your finance team.

Call suggestion: Wed 13 May, 10:00–10:30 PT to walk legal + procurement through the MAP. Does that work?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
